interactions.title: Shadow armor and the Night Queen
lines: Kenzo: So as, as you know, this may be Delwath, you— if you and I—you and Kenzo— are sort of binding up the orc, on you know Kenzo just kind of like looking over at you a little bit. Yeah you're wearing your shadow armor, right? Yep. And looking over, it's like, "So you aren't a shadow warrior of Shakun's, right? That's like you were not that, right?"

Kenzo: Okay, but you don't you really don't know—like, this is just casual conversation as we're binding up the orc—you guys, you really you really don't know where you were, where all this came from?
Delwath: The armor was the armor I wore in the battles against the Great War.

Kenzo: But it wasn't shadow armor? Yeah it was just normal armor, right? Like it didn't have the whole black cast, yeah, you know, that would make me think that you're a shadow warrior? I mean, I know you're not. I mean, I think I know you're not.

Seeker: And is all darkness evil? Is all evil to be found in darkness? Maybe, but maybe there's more to the world than we know. Or, conversely, perhaps this prediction what can happen to Delwath, even though it seems unlikely... I

Kenzo: I feel like it's within the spectrum of possible. Now, I don't hold it against you, just to be clear about that, though. It's not something—I have no personal, you know, interactions. It feels like you know you're you're actually a liberator of the Great War, so I you know I don't really... Do, but—curious.

Seeker: What, what are some association? Now, I've already purple gem goggle inspected the armor without any further insight, but I'm curious if we knew anything about the lore of shadows suggesting that there are—oh yeah, actually, turning to you—cultures, traditions, gods that somehow connected to shadows? Yeah.

DM: There's—I mean there's lots of myths about shadows, right? Like shadows are associated with the fey. They're associated with um, you know there's plenty of of you know stories of, you know, the things that come out at night, and of course they're not all evil. Right, I mean there's undead, there's like malicious things, but there's also you know fairies and you know wights and things like that, and, you know it's not, I would say.

DM: There's not like a god that is you know, particularly, certainly in the Dunmari culture... There's not a—there's not a god that is really strongly associated with shadow, although you do remember from growing up in Chardon, there is one of the set of that sort of dominant religion outside of, of, of Dunmar, is the Eight Divines, sometimes called the way or or Mos Numena. And there is a god associated with that tradition, the Night Queen, who is seen as kind of the—you know the one who is watches over transitions and shadows and twilight. And so, from your childhood, you would you would you know not...
DM: I mean, this is not your—you know, since you've met Kaeso. I mean, you were never religious, right? You were a street urchin.
DM: Guys know, but… you would know these things, right? And so...

before: Unknown: Hmm.
Seeker: So we set about binding the...
DM: He's unconscious, so it's easy to get him tied up.
Kenzo: Okay, as a start, maybe, maybe Delwath, are you helping them? [garbled].
Delwath: And Delwath is helping.
after: Kenzo: And then I mean Kenzo has no like particular prejudice or anything like that, you know, obviously. Delwath has been like killing things with like weird demonic swords, you know—not demonic swords, [garbled] going to be evil. Evil energy. Evil—what? There's the energy, but anyways, Kenzo's just just, you know...

Seeker: I like how we're having this casual conversation about good and evil while tying up an orc. Um I I pulled the little notebook out of a deeply buried pocket among my things and and pull it open and say, "I did one time write down the word Shadowfell. I think that might have been, Delwath, where you said you were imprisoned, but I don't know much more about what it is. Is that the place you were held?"
Delwath: I don't know if it was Shadowfell, although Shadowfell is the shadowy echo of the Feywild.
Seeker: I quickly set about adding to my notes.
Delwath: But I don't know much of it. I know my people, much—many, many years ago, used to travel to the Feywild, but it's not something I ever did.

interactions.title: Havdar’s thanks and the orc threat
lines: DM: Yep, okay. So you sort of roughly slings—you know you're all pretty weak, but between two of you, you can sort of manage to manhandle the orc down to—down the—off the side of a cliff. So the you know the canyon sort of slopes down a bit, so you go around the long way and then and then come, you know, down into Havdar's camp. And, as you come down to the camp, you can see you know this looking pretty rough. Like there's some you know there's it looks like four of Havdar's warriors are dead, and a number are badly wounded. And he is you know, after having sort of cleaned himself up, he is sort of just going around to his troops, you know sort of offering words of support encouragement. But when he sees you you know coming down, especially with the orc, he walks over to you.

DM: And he is—I mean, he— you've not seen him really shaken before, but he seems a little bit shaken and says, "Glad you arrived when you did. Not sure we could have held off another one of those fire blasts from that spell caster. Not expecting that from orcs. I thank you greatly."

DM: No, we were not ambushed. I was just not expecting fireballs. The one who was slinging fire around like I—like it was his personal toy was... Not sure we would have gotten up up to the top of the canyon in time to to deal with him before he just dropped rain fire down on us from above. They are...
Kenzo: But I mean, did they surprise you?

DM: We killed a group of about 20 orcs coming—20–25 orcs coming from the north through the canyon. And this small band slaughtered our—our watch on our left flank and snuck around, attacked us from above while we were arrayed against the larger band coming through the canyon.
DM: It was a—again, a battle plan of sophistication I would not have...
Seeker: Expected from these such creatures. A coordinated trap.
Seeker: Um, Tim, do we know anything about like orcs and their like spell casting abilities?

DM: So yeah, I mean you know the sort of standard story about orcs, right? Is that they're the kind of—their, you know in thrall to the to this god of endless war, and so you know, many of them have some divine spell casting ability. Orcs like sorcerous orcs are not something that you have heard of before.
Wellby: I nod toward the standard, like the emblems. And so, Havdar, but everyone else too, have you seen this standard before?
DM: Not this particular one. I mean these foul creatures always have some standard or or name they fight under. Um. This one is unfamiliar to me.
Wellby: I look over to Delwath.
Delwath: I assume I don't recognize the standard, now.

DM: While you're sort of standing there, he—the sort of tall, older man with unkempt graying hair who was walking around before walks over, and Havdar introduces him. He says, "This is Aram. He's a holy warrior of Aagir." And they talk for a moment and—seems to be asked—is—seems to be saying that they're preparing to say blessings and cremate the four dead warriors, and he wants Havdar to say a few words when when he has a chance. There is going to be a small funeral. He also wants, he also asked Havdar, "What should we do with the orc bodies?" Havdar's like, "Drag them in a pile, I guess. Deal with them later."
Kenzo: Anybody in your party speak orc or common, knows how to communicate?
DM: Yeah, we can. I've picked up some bits of their language in my travels.
DM: Some speak the common tongue as well. When he wakes, can see.

Wellby: Havdar, the the band of 20 that you're engaged with—the ones we saw up on the ridge didn't have gear supplies for long journey in the desert. They weren't carrying food or water. What about these?

DM: No, I think they must have set a camp further up the canyon. I've sent some scouts to go that track back their trails quietly, make sure there's not more waiting to ambush us in the night. If there are, we’ll know soon. If there's a camp, we must find the signs of that.
Seeker: Are we vulnerable down here in the canyon? Should we get to higher ground?

DM: So good question, I mean, we may consider moving our camp up to the ridge, set up a system to bring up the water as needed. The canyon is sheltered from the—from the heat, shady during the hot—hottest part of the day.
Seeker: Used to be in this palm tree up there, but...
DM: Several of my scouts are still out riding. I hope—I anticipate they'll be back sometime tomorrow anyway. Is this all the orcs? Are there more? I don't know.
Kenzo: Especially the other ones that we were dealing with—at least, is the only one we captured.
DM: That's good. I saw you fought well up there.
DM: Greatly appreciated. Aid coming unlooked unlooked for is sometimes the best aid of all.
Kenzo: The Havdar, what do you make of all this?
DM: I would hear what this foul creature has to say, if we can get it to talk.
Kenzo: We met, we met… we met a, you know, you know, what's the name of the kid again?

Kenzo: You know, as we know, when we visited Amil's mentors, they told us some interesting things about the orcs. They told us that the orcs have been peaceful, that they had been—set up a society for themselves and were—were not—were not attacking.
DM: I don't know. I've never heard of such a thing.
Kenzo: Did you say that the orcs attack you, or did you attack the orcs?
Delwath: Amil's masters also said the orcs had been fighting each other, right? Am I misremembering that, Tim?
Delwath: Yeah, that's right, that—a new clan, perhaps, attacking the peaceful ones.
Kenzo: These markings, the rising sun—what is a clerk—that mean anything to you?
DM: As I said, they always have marks. Screaming face, the burning sun, call themselves things like this, but...

DM: Listen, the sun is beginning to set. I think in an hour or so, my—my troops will be ready for the funeral of those who died. Should we wake this orc now, or would you like to interrogate it in the morning?

before: DM: Not carrying much. I mean they you know, not much rations or anything. They must have either—they have some magical way of getting food, or they must have a camp somewhere and have left from that camp to come here, or somebody else was carrying the food. These are you know, obviously a battle party, relatively light and in gear other than their weapons and armor. But you don't really find much else or notice much else.
Seeker: To search with eyes open next.
Delwath: Let’s, um...
Kenzo: Havdar—bring the orc.
Wellby: Yeah, bring the orc.
after: DM: Um he signals—he, he goes walks over to to Aram, the the tall, older guy, and and brings them over, and, like they have a quick whispered conversation, and Aram looks a little skeptical, but he places his his hand on the shoulder of the orc and you know start saying under his breath, "Aagir's spirit bring you back." And the orc like shudders awake as sort of a little glow on his hand, and snaps his eyes open, starts looking around, like growling at the crowd. Aram kind of jumps back, then realizes the orc is tied up, and Havdar—Havdar then like turns to you. "Anything you want to know?"
Seeker: Why did they attack?
Delwath: Where have they been to recently?
Wellby: Who do they serve?
Seeker: Who do they serve?

interactions.title: Reviving and questioning Gorkil
lines: DM: Um he signals—he, he goes walks over to to Aram, the the tall, older guy, and and brings them over, and, like they have a quick whispered conversation, and Aram looks a little skeptical, but he places his his hand on the shoulder of the orc and you know start saying under his breath, "Aagir's spirit bring you back." And the orc like shudders awake as sort of a little glow on his hand, and snaps his eyes open, starts looking around, like growling at the crowd. Aram kind of jumps back, then realizes the orc is tied up, and Havdar—Havdar then like turns to you. "Anything you want to know?"
Delwath: Where have they been to recently?

DM: That the orc starts laughing, in this sort of maniacal laugh behind you as you're talking, and um, starts just kind of like looking at you, Wellby, you said, "Who do you serve?" And says in in common, not in Dunmari, but in the sort of trade tongue, you know, "You want to know who we serve? Grash, the blighted one. You will serve him too."
Kenzo: Where is Grash? Where can we find Grash?
DM: You seek to join Grash's worship?
Delwath: Is Grash though the god all the orcs worship? No?
Kenzo: Have you ever heard of Grash?
DM: If you serve Grash, you will never die.
Delwath: Who is the guy—what's the god? Is it—I forget the name of the god that I'll be…
DM: The god of war without end.
Delwath: Grash—is not Thark angry you've abandoned him?
DM: He like spits on the ground by your feet. Ah, "Thark is weak. Thark is—does not speak to me, does not speak to us."
DM: He looks over at you. "Why should I speak to you, unfaithful?"
Delwath: Are you not a prophet of Grash, with with...?
Delwath: Are you not here to spread his word?
DM: Yes, Grash can use servants of all races. Grash will make you strong. Grash will make you never die. When you die, you will rise 10 times stronger, again and again. The glory of Grash!
Wellby: And when—Wellby, I lean in. "I haven't before met an orc afraid to speak of this."

DM: Like struggles against his bonds and, like, "I am not afraid! Grash, he speaks to us. One year. Many years, Uzgash's bastards wander the desert, living in peace." He spits on the ground again. "So we turned away from those weaklings."
Delwath: And where did you find Grash? He must have come to you in a powerful place.
DM: Came to us. The city of the dead rulers. The city with the big tombs lurking over it.
DM: You come to him. He will welcome you. You will never die.
Wellby: Where in the city can we find him?
DM: The darkest place in the heart of the city. The undying dwells there. Only the brave can make it, dodging the ghosts. He blesses us.
Wellby: What did he ask in return?
DM: Kill Uzgash's brats. Take their treasure. Bring it to him.
Seeker: I gesture to the shield. "Is this the sign of Grash, the rising sun, the screaming face?"
DM: Yes. And now kill me so I can rise again.
Kenzo: Kenzo's kind of sort of like quickly at this: "Is Grash stronger than Shakun?"
DM: Who's Shakun? Grash is stronger than all.
Wellby: I'll turn to Havdar and just say, "We should probably burn the bodies."
DM: Havdar looks over at at Aram. He says...
Kenzo: Like—like, right now. We should prepare to burn the bodies.

Seeker: Tim, what do you—what do I—do we know anything about like this thing of like rising again 10 times stronger? Is that is that, like a thing, or maybe just a story that he's told? There—if so, is there a way we could prevent it, if it's real?

DM: I mean. Ah yeah, go ahead and roll Arcana. It's—it's, you know, there's like plenty of stories like this, right? I mean, so, Seeker, you’ve read—you haven't you know deeply studied the nature of undead, but you've certainly spent enough time in the dwarven archives sort of reading about just all sorts of legends and myths about different kinds of creatures that that you certainly come across stories of...
DM: You know the thing that's the most similar that you've come across are like you know stories of creatures like zombies that you know rise up from the bodies of the dead.

DM: You know the sort of "10 times stronger" thing, well, you know it's a little bit hard to tell if that is meaningful. There are certainly—there certainly are magic's that can create—that can, that can animate the dead—dead bodies and and bring them back.

DM: Something that could work at a great distance would be unusual in your experience, but not completely unheard of. You know, far more likely to you would be that, this far away from whoever this Grash is, probably this is just a myth. But maybe closer, maybe in the city, maybe closer to his lair, he actually has the power to do this. That would be your take on things.
Delwath: Did you succeed at killing that Uzgash?
DM: Of course we succeed. We are strong. We are Grash's warriors. The blighted one wins all battles.
Delwath: I point over to the dead orcs. "All battles?"
DM: This battle is not over yet, for… and he starts laughing again.
Delwath: How mighty is he? Does he rule all the orcs, the thousands?
DM: We will be thousand soon enough. Growth. Uzgash, Uzgash's strength. Soon all will be Grash. Are there more Grash's?
Seeker: Are there more of your fire casters?
DM: Grash blesses us with many powers.
DM: Strong. He like sort of throws out his neck. "Kill me and you will see."
Seeker: Maybe we should keep you around. Maybe you'll see your chance to kill yourself and take over from him.
DM: Haha. I am strong. I do not think such blasphemy.
DM: Blasphemer! You will be the first to die.
Wellby: What else dwells in the dead city of the rulers?
DM: Grash rules all. What Grash wants, Grash brings.
Delwath: How long has a—Grash—Grash has been there a year?
Kenzo: Are we burning these bodies?

DM: Yeah, Aram has already gone over to do that. He's like dragging, building a fire. Havdar's just kind of watching this, but he motioned Aram over as soon as you suggested that and started burning the bodies.
Seeker: What is your name, faithful one?
DM: I am Gorkil. I will kill you later.
Delwath: Disappointed about that one, Gorkil.
Wellby: How is it that you've come so far through the desert without food and water?
Seeker: Wellby with the actual useful questions.
DM: The desert is ours. We camp where we want. We raid where we want.
DM: Why should I tell you that?
Wellby: It doesn't matter. We'll just follow your tracks back anyways.

before: Kenzo: Before, before we leave, just metagame: like Kenzo—well, we’ll grab like a stretch of like you know, like whatever summit, you know, like one of the orcs has probably got that on like a you know piece of fabric, whatever. Just like… Just grab that and keep it up.

DM: Listen, the sun is beginning to set. I think in an hour or so, my—my troops will be ready for the funeral of those who died. Should we wake this orc now, or would you like to interrogate it in the morning?
Wellby: Now.
Unknown: Now.
Kenzo: There you have it.
after: Seeker: Think about whether it's worth casting suggestion on him to persuade him to tell us something specific, but it's not obvious that there's something that we need to know that he does.
Kenzo: Well, maybe we sidebar in Dunmari, for—or just the us. They can't hear us for a moment.
Wellby: Well, can we sidebar telepathically? To—sorry to cut you off, but, like, can we sidebar telepathically? Do we have to do that verbally?
DM: Um yeah, your telepathy, it's not a—it's not a group chat.
Wellby: Can't conference you in.

interactions.title: Shakun’s silence and the risks of planar travel
lines: Kenzo: Um. Okay, so I guess we can talk back back in game. I think for us to really figure out what the fuck is going on, we need to figure out how to communicate directly with the gods.

Kenzo: What are we doing here? This is—Shakun has gone. Our god is gone. You know, for us to understand what's really happening, there's—there's—there's another game, there's a—there's another level of the game, and we need to be able to understand what that is. Otherwise we're just playing in the dark.
Delwath: Are these gods really gone, or can people here just not hear them? I think if the god of the orcs had vanished from Taelgar a year ago, more would have changed.
Kenzo: Fine, not not necessarily have left, but whatever is happening on our plane is is trickled down from some politics that we are as of yet—is—it is opaque to us.
Delwath: No, I mean, do we know if the gods have left, or there's a wall and they can't get through?
Delwath: Or it could even be be here. Something in this place that is preventing the the gods from... But clearly not all gods.

Delwath: Well, do we know that the orcs in the far north cannot hear their god? Do you think that orcs in Chardon cannot hear that god? Literally—literally [garbled]. Delwath points over to the healer. "If the gods are truly gone, he wouldn't be able to heal us."
Wellby: Look, this is a conversation to have with Candrosa.
Delwath: Do we know, I mean, that is interesting. Has Candrosa done any magic since we...?
Wellby: Have magically evaded our questions.
Delwath: But he hasn't actually cast any spells, has he?
DM: Zone of truth on you.
Delwath: Did cast zone of truth on us.
DM: But that was a while ago.
Seeker: After the fall of the...
DM: Yes, it was after the fall of Karawa.
Seeker: So he's not completely devoid of that power. Does that power come directly from Shakun?
Wellby: Or if he's turned to another god.
Delwath: I mean, I guess, if he's calling himself a paladin—is now serving some other master...

Seeker: Kenzo, I have to admit I have that same wish to make a kind of leap. I wish to find the interconnections between the planes and travel among them, and even to communicate with these gods and meddle in their politics, as you're suggesting. But I have to admit to reflecting on the loss of my younger brother, that he meddled with something that maybe he should not have, and so there could be costs.
Seeker: Might want to beware that kind of thing without proper...
Delwath: I must say I have very—well, no desire to travel the outer planes and get trapped in another dimension.

Kenzo: Look, I'm not saying that I necessarily want myself or for us be the ones that go there. What I'm saying is we're spending a lot of fucking time and effort killing a lot of orcs, killing a lot of weird demons. And we're spending a lot of effort right now, I think, in ways that aren't necessarily helping us understand the true game that's being played. Now, to understand the true game that's being played, we may not have to go there ourselves. Maybe there's some conduits. And I agree, Wellby, I think Candrosa... He has—he still has tales to tell us, and he actually—they have the one artifact that can get us into the Plane of Dreams, which is the one, one place we could go, because...

Seeker: He's under some kind of curse. I think, personally, that we've seen hints that somewhere in Dunmar is hidden knowledge. We've got to keep asking around and searching—the—the ideas, and maybe the power, are here within our grasp.

before: DM: But how you go there without dying is, ah, it's a little bit not all—I mean it's unclear how one actually would do that. There are legends, but none of them...
DM: And there are stories I mean the gods coming here as well, right? Obviously, if Laka and Bhishma had a child, they had to be in the same place together at one point.
Delwath: Well, depends on the power of god, but...
Unknown: True.

DM: So there's definitely you know stories of of beings going back and forth in a sort of physical way between the planes, but it's not—none of the stories are very specific on how one would actually go about doing that. Well.
after: Unknown: Yeah.
Delwath: It would be interesting to know a bit more about this Grash.
Seeker: Like what?
Delwath: Is Grash a mighty wizard, a true god, a fey creature, a dragon?
Seeker: It would be interesting. Suppose Grash was a, say, human. Probably know. Grash could be a female dwarf.

interactions.title: Gorkil describes Grash’s spirits and enemies
lines: Wellby: Well, ask the orc then. "Describe to us Grash. You saw it."
DM: You're done with your babbling? Spits again, he’s like spitting blood out of his like battered face. "I grow weary. I wish to be reborn in glory. You are wasting my time."
Wellby: The faster you tell us, the sooner you move on.
DM: Grash is mighty. He is a dark spirit in the heart of the city. Strong. Everywhere and nowhere. He speaks to us. He blesses us with his might.
Delwath: You seen him, been in his presence?
DM: I have not been so blessed. I have been near him.
Delwath: You know the—those who have been so blessed?
DM: When I am reborn, I will be strong enough, yes. I will be in his presence, and he will help me kill you, blasphemer! Looking at Seeker.
Seeker: I look a little nervous.
Wellby: I point to Seeker. "Him in particular?"
Seeker: Well, I did proactively blaspheme. Yes, that's correct.
DM: He suggested killing Grash. One does not kill a power such as his.
Delwath: No, we're not—what? How would he stop us?
DM: We are strong. He commands all the haunted spirits of the city. And he will not stop till he has the treasure he seeks.
Wellby: Where were you going when you tried to kill all these humans? You're going somewhere.
DM: Killing humans is motive enough.
Wellby: What treasure? You're going west. So, nor…
DM: My travels are no business of yours.
Wellby: Did you hear what happened at Raven's Hold?
DM: Such things have no meaning to me. Raven's Hold? I care not for those words.
Wellby: What's her name is hold? I look to Seeker, like, is there a name for it in orcish? There must be.
Delwath: It was hob-goblins there, not...
Wellby: Oh, it was a hobgoblin. And there was the one orc up there, though.
DM: Orc. You saw one orc, yep.
Kenzo: Yeah remember the markings on that orc?
DM: Ah, interesting. Did not seem to have any, know, like tattoos or anything. Well much more like...
Delwath: How do you find Uzgash? You must be a skilled tracker to find them.
DM: They are easy to find. They grow food and build farms and keep animals. They are weak, pathetic. We will slaughter them and bring their treasure back to—back to Grash, and he will grow stronger.
Wellby: Yeah, and then what, though? Play that forward.
DM: And I will be your lord and master, and you will bow before Grash.
Wellby: So, not really thought this one through.
Delwath: You're seeking treasure for Grash?
Delwath: So—oh go ahead. What sort of treasure?
DM: You have tribute for Grash to give me? I will take it to him. He wants all the treasures across the land.

Delwath: I hear there's a there's an old woman in the in the west, collects these things. Perhaps you could go—send your troops that way and see if you could get her treasure. The Dustmother, I believe she's called.
DM: She is weak. Grash will kill her.
Delwath: If he hasn't yet, she can't be that weak.
DM: Grash is strong, and he will kill her when the time is right.
Delwath: When he gets strong enough to be able to, you mean?
DM: He could kill her whenever he wanted to.
DM: You're clearly like flustering him a little bit. "Not question Grash, blasphemers! When this battle is finished, I will dance on your graves."

DM: You now can see over his shoulder like flickering fires of a giant pyre, as Aram and Havdar have finished dragging the orcs' bodies on to this just giant like pile, fed by the palm tree that was knocked down in the battle, which they have dragged from the tops of the cliffs and chopped up for wood. And the sun is beginning to set as the smoke rises, and you can smell the burning flesh of the orcs being charred and turned to ash.
Wellby: Other humans besides these horse people wandering in these parts?
DM: We kill them. Kill any we see.
Kenzo: Are you holding any captive in Kharsan?
DM: Pack—captives? Waste of food. Better to eat them.
Kenzo: And if we were to give you a tribute to go to Kharsan, would would Grash kill us then too?
DM: If you serve him, he will not kill you. We serve him and he does not kill us. Once Grash blesses you, you are his.
Wellby: He sent you here to die.
Seeker: So, Kenzo, are you thinking like elaborate orc outfits?
Delwath: I think Grash might be able to see through such things. Or at least I don't think Grash cares if we're orcs or not, but he's gonna know if we're not really there to serve him, right?
Seeker: I think we probably have gotten what we can get out of this guy.
Kenzo: Kenzo takes the staff, like the hobgoblin the staff from the... And he pulls it out and gives it to the orc. "Think Grash would like this as tribute?"
Kenzo: It's true. It's not that fancy, Kenzo.
DM: Grash will take any tribute. Anything old, especially.
Kenzo: Why does he like old things?
Delwath: Because he's working for the—I'll say this in Dunmari—is he in league with the Chardonian Order of the Open Hand?
Kenzo: Why does he want old things?
DM: Old things are strong. Grash is strong. Old things make him stronger. Take the treasures of everyone. Take...
DM: Take that—Uzgash's brats. Take their ore, take their loot, claim it for us.
DM: They live all over. They have vermin paths.
Delwath: I think we should find—I'll say this in Dunmari—so I think we should find Uzgash.

before: Unknown: Yeah.
Delwath: It would be interesting to know a bit more about this Grash.
Seeker: Like what?
